gen_cost._doc: What a generation costs, so a sheet can be budgeted before it is fired. THREE MCP SERVERS AND TWO TIER LADDERS: gpt-image-2 (1k) and gpt-image-2-2k run the OLD model on the OLD ladder and nothing already generated against them changes meaning; gpt-image-25 (1k only) runs gpt-image-2.5. 2.5 KEPT EVERY PRICE AND MOVED THE LABELS - 2.5 'high' spends what gpt-image-2 'medium' spent and 2.5 'max' spends what gpt-image-2 'high' spent, so a tier name carried across servers means something else. Every texture in this file was generated at gpt-image-2 'medium' = 1,756 output tokens; on 2.5 that is 'high', which is why that is the 2.5 server's default. MEASURED HERE, not quoted: three separate 1024x1024 gpt-image-2 'medium' calls each returned output_tokens exactly 1756, and output tokens do not move with prompt length (input ran 757-1003 across the three).

gpt-image-2.5._note: Identical price at every tier. Flare is the fast default; Sunburst is 1.5-2x slower and claims tighter layout and edit control - the one to reach for on a pack sheet, where layout adherence is the whole game. Tokens at 1024x1024; the per-tier counts are third-party measurement (CellCog 2026-09-08) since OpenAI publishes only the $/1M rates and says its own calculator does not cover 2.5. The 'high' row is corroborated: gpt-image-2 'medium' measured 1756 here, and the re-grade puts 2.5 'high' at that same spend.

gpt-image-2._note: The old ladder, unchanged. Still the only 2k route. 'medium' is what everything in this file was generated at.

per_cell_usd_at_parity_tier._note: One 1024 generation split into a grid, at the 1,756-token tier ($0.0527). art_px_per_object is what the cell is actually WORTH - cell px x the median long-axis fill measured on a real drop. Divide THAT by the world size the thing is DRAWN at to get texels/unit, and that second step is what picks the grid: a 2.43-unit bench billboard needs 6x6 or better (facility/floor-tile is 73 texels/unit), while a 0.75-unit flat decal on emitted geometry is fine at 8x8 and gets 64 subjects for one generation. Verified on the PACKED sheets rather than the drops: median largest-blob share 1.0000 on both, no clip artefacts from --tol 4, borders_nonzero 0 - raw-drop misalignment never survives the packer, so do not reject a dense grid on how the drop looks.

style: STYLE — match style-flat.png: a flat-shaded stylized texture for a top-down moody-night roguelike. Matte flat colors, very dark and muted desaturated palette, low contrast, even flat ambient lighting, subtle fine film grain, simple clean shapes, minimal detail. ABSOLUTELY NO photorealism, no realistic or volumetric lighting, no glossy/specular reflections, no lens or camera effects, no soft photographic shadows or depth of field — it should look hand-painted and flat, like a 2D game tile.
style_prop: STYLE — match style-flat.png: a flat-shaded stylized object for a top-down moody-night roguelike. Matte flat colors, even flat ambient lighting, subtle fine film grain, simple clean shapes, minimal detail. The object's own manufactured colour must READ AS THAT COLOUR — keep it clearly saturated at a medium-dark value, do not grey it out, do not wash it toward the background. ABSOLUTELY NO photorealism, no realistic or volumetric lighting, no glossy/specular reflections, no lens or camera effects, no soft photographic shadows or depth of field — it should look hand-painted and flat, like a 2D game tile.
_style_doc: TWO strings, and which one you append depends on what the image IS. `style` is for a SURFACE — a tiling texture, a decal, a sprite sheet: a wall really is grey, so its 'very dark and muted desaturated palette, low contrast' clause is correct there and every one of the 203 shipped textures wears it. `style_prop` is for an OBJECT — a TRELLIS reference image, i.e. anything that becomes a glb: it is the same string with that one clause replaced by the opposite instruction, because an object's colour is a fact about the object and a manufactured thing that comes back grey is simply wrong. Measured before the split: 9 of 38 props carried a per-channel `baseColor` and every one of them shipped neutral, `wild/tree-broadleaf-full` losing a 41.5-chroma green canopy to 3.8 and `facility/trash-bin` a bottle-green body to 0.1. Append ONE of them verbatim to EVERY gpt-image-2 gen/edit prompt; keep both in sync with the texture-art-style memory, and keep every clause but the palette one identical between them.
_doc: Source-of-truth for textures. src lives in textures-src/ (1024), output goes to textures/<label>.png. class: tile|window|chroma|sprite. needs_alpha -> tool warns if output is opaque. chroma -> key color baked to alpha before downscale. prompt_exact:false means the prompt was reconstructed, not the original. Run `make tex` after editing a source or this file.
